---
title: "Method"
subtitle: "Compare each fire building with similar buildings on its own block, using only earlier records"
---

## The comparison

1. **Cases.** Buildings HPD ordered vacated for fire damage (pilot: January 2025).
2. **Comparison buildings.** Residential buildings on the same block, of similar size
   (from about a third to three times as many apartments), built before 2000. Same-block
   matching holds neighborhood, era and building stock roughly constant.
3. **Records before the event only.** Every count uses records dated before the cutoff
   (pilot: January 1, 2025). The full study adds a 60-day gap before each fire.
4. **Rank within the block.** Each case's value is ranked against its own neighbors
   (0% = lowest on the block, 100% = highest, ties split).
5. **Test against chance.** A permutation test repeatedly picks a random building on each block
   as a fake "case." The p-value is the share of 20,000 shuffles whose average rank is as high
   as the real cases'.

## Signals measured (pilot)

| Signal | Source | Scaled by size |
|---|---|---|
| Class C ("immediately hazardous") violations | HPD | per apartment |
| All A, B and C violations | HPD | per apartment |
| Smoke and CO detector violations | HPD (text search) | per apartment |
| Registration failures (Class I) | HPD | no |
| Maintenance, emergency, unsafe-building and uncertified-hazard violations | DOB | no |
| Missed boiler filings | DOB | no |

## Known biases

- **Inspection intensity.** Violations exist only where someone inspected, and inspections follow
  tenant complaints. A building with organized tenants can look worse than a neglected building
  whose tenants don't call.
- **Coverage.** HPD covers rental housing; one- and two-family owner-occupied homes rarely appear.
- **Timing.** Violations written right after a fire can look like warnings unless records near the
  event are excluded.
- **Small samples.** The pilot has 7 fire cases and 9 collapse cases.

## Full-study plan

Conditional logistic regression on matched sets (the standard model for this design), a
machine-learning pass (LightGBM with SHAP explanations) to find combinations, and a temporal
holdout: fit on 2018–2023 fires, then test how well the signals rank 2024–2025 fires.
